newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans extend gains on oversold signals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans extend gains on oversold signals.

text.p: Gains were extended late in CBOT soybean futures amid signals the market was oversold and talk that export business was in the works, traders said.
"It's just oversold," a trader said. "There's business being done, according to the rumor mill, and some people are saying we've put in the seasonal lows for new crop."

Talk circulated in the market that China was looking to buy U.S. old and new crop soybeans and Brazil and Argentina were interested in new crop U.S. supplies. U.S. exporters could not confirm the rumors.

Floor sources also pointed to bullish concensus figures for May 27 which showed a drop to 47 percent from 65 percent the previous week. Some traders suggested the sharp break was overdone and signalled the market was due for a recovery.
At 1256 CDT, soybeans were up 12-1/4 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel with July up 12-1/4 at $8.43-1/2.
